Git Workflow.B: Create a GitHub organisation; invite Akash, Hemachandran and Siva
Create private repository vi-websync-ai with Python and Node .gitignore
Create develop branch from main; protect main and develop
Create folder structure from documentation section 7; commit
Add pull request template and CODEOWNERS file
Create labels: phase-0 to phase-5, ui, backend, ai, integration, bug
Clone the repository; run docker compose up; confirm the stack starts
main = released code only. develop = integration branch. Work on feature/<task-id>-short-name, for example feature/T036-annotation-canvas. Hotfixes use hotfix/<name> from main.
Start with a type: feat, fix, test, docs, refactor or chore. Include the task ID, for example: feat(T036): add polygon editing
One task per PR. Aim for under 400 changed lines. Fill in the PR template and link the Task ID.
One approval from the code owner. Reviews within 4 working hours. Authors resolve every comment before merge.
apps/web/ = Hemachandran. services/api/, services/worker/, infra/ = Siva. ai/, services/inference/, services/edge-agent/, packages/labview/ = Akash. packages/schemas/ = any two approvals.
No direct pushes to main or develop. CI must pass before merge.
Never commit keys, passwords, model weights or customer images. Use .env.example and GitHub Secrets.
Model weights and datasets live in object storage. Use Git LFS only for small sample assets.
Use a GitHub Projects board with columns Backlog, To do, In progress, In review, Done. Mirror the Task Board sheet.
Friday: develop is tagged as a release candidate. Merge to main only after acceptance tests pass.
